name: checkpoints
summary: Supervised-build checkpoints: a fresh-context supervisor grades the plan at session-open, the diff at pre-commit, and the demonstration at milestone-close, in a fixed verdict vocabulary.

action.none: No honest matcher. The CATEGORY is committing with the local hooks bypassed, and its spellings are unbounded shell: `--no-verify`, the `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null` form that an incident in this repository actually used, `core.hooksPath` set at any config origin beforehand, `HUSKY=0` and its equivalents, or a wrapper on PATH. This rule carried `git commit --no-verify` for one milestone, and in the measured incident that matcher gave ZERO protection while reading as coverage — the act performed was the same category in another spelling, so the gate as enumerated never reached it. A matcher covering one spelling of an unbounded set is worse than an honest gap, because only the gap is visible. Enforcement here is the reader's discipline under the rule that an act's absence from a list is not a finding of permission (`core/operating/autonomy.md`); the incident is recorded as incident 3 of `.portulan/proposals/0029-a-constraint-names-a-category-not-a-list.md`.

gates.reason: Bypassing the local hooks — by any spelling — turns a compiled gate back into a convention on a workspace that compiles its gate policy into those hooks. If the hooks are wrong, change the policy through the evolution gate rather than stepping around it for one commit: a bypass leaves no trace in the record that a policy change would have left.

action.none: No tool-level surface, and naming it rather than inventing a matcher is the point. A checkpoint verdict is a paragraph written into a record, so the act of grading your own work is indistinguishable at the tool layer from the act of recording someone else's grade. What makes the rule real is the fresh context, which no permission rule can observe — see the honest-limits section of README.md.

gates.reason: The context that did the work may not also supply the verdict on it. A supervisor sharing the implementer's window has already read every rationalisation the implementer wrote for itself, which is the failure the fresh-context requirement exists to prevent, and a verdict produced that way looks exactly like one that was not.
